key_insight: TRACE is a unified, energy-conserving interatomic potential that pairs ACE density correlations with local cross-attention to model many-body chemistry and crystal physics without passing learned states between atoms.
engineering_relevance: It offers a scalable route to accurate molecular dynamics on a laptop-class machine, supporting phase transitions, liquid structure, and reaction barriers with one architecture.
method: ACE-based O(3)-equivariant center states capture many-body density correlations.
Local multihead cross-attention queries fixed tensorial neighbor features determined by species and geometry.
No learned message passing state is propagated between atoms, preserving energy conservation and efficiency.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on polymorphic cesium lead iodide, liquid water, and methyl migration, matching key experimental or high-level reference targets such as a ~580 K phase crossing, an O–O distance of 2.85 Å, and a 27.92±0.03 kcal/mol barrier.
watch_item: Performance may depend on high-quality reference data and enhanced sampling for rare transitions, so transferability outside the demonstrated chemistries and phase spaces remains to be validated.
